items.claim: Jer.17.5-17.11 is typed judgment_oracle under the closed unit_type vocabulary, but the span's own operative-category deviation (its literature_type_guess calls the material 'wisdom-toned') is not disclosed anywhere in device_notes, which addresses only parashah marks.
items.evidence: No category in the controlled unit_type list names wisdom material, so judgment_oracle is a defensible closest fit for the curse-and-consequence shape of the cursed/blessed pair (Jer.17.5-8) and the ill-gotten-riches saying (Jer.17.11), but the one-sentence disclosure of that operative-category deviation belongs in device_notes and is absent there; device_notes covers only the setumah marks at Jer.17.4, 17.6, and 17.10, byte-confirmed against the MT parashah inventory.
tier_citations: controlled unit_type vocabulary (13-value, no wisdom category)
MT parashah inventory (single-witness, tier-3 weak, Prophets)

items.claim: Jer.17.12-17.13 correctly stands alone as hymn_doxology on a genuine speaker/addressee shift on both edges, not on the closing setumah, which is cited only as texture.
items.evidence: No koh-amar or word-event formula falls in Jer.17.12-13; the cut from the preceding third-person generic wisdom material to first-person-plural sanctuary address, and onward from this span's own third-person description of those who forsake Yahweh to Jer.17.14's first-person individual petition, is a genuine speaker-focus shift on both edges, byte-confirmed against the collated text; the setumah at Jer.17.13 is disclosed as single-witness tier-3 texture, not as the driver.

items.claim: Jer.17.14-17.18 stands as a self-contained individual confession, opened and closed by a genuine speaker-focus seam with no interior tier-1 marker calling for a split.
items.evidence: The span carries no koh-amar or word-event formula; its first-person address to Yahweh runs unbroken from the healing plea (Jer.17.14) through the persecution imprecation (Jer.17.18), distinct from the third-person doxology preceding it and the fresh commission scene opening at Jer.17.19; the surrounding setumah marks at Jer.17.13 and Jer.17.18 are correctly disclosed as tier-3 texture rather than as boundary drivers.

items.claim: Jer.17.19-17.27 is correctly held as one commissioned prose sermon; the interior koh-amar at Jer.17.21 continues the same frame owner and the same addressee already fixed at Jer.17.19-20 rather than opening a fresh unit.
items.evidence: koh-amar recurs at Jer.17.19 and Jer.17.21 with no frame-owner change; Jer.17.20 fixes the addressee as the kings of Judah, all Judah, and Jerusalem's inhabitants, and Jer.17.21 continues addressing that same group through the Sabbath prohibition rather than naming anyone new; the whole span is prose throughout with zero WEB poetry-line verses, matching prose_sermon rather than the poetry dominating the confession and wisdom material earlier in the chapter; the closing petuchah at Jer.17.27 is disclosed as tier-3 texture, correctly not used as the boundary's driver.

items.claim: Jer.18.1-18.12 correctly holds the potter's-house command, performance, interpretation, and application to Judah as one symbolic-act unit; the interior word-event formula at Jer.18.5 and the koh-amar-plus-addressee turn at Jer.18.11 both fall inside the act's own interpretation stage rather than opening an independent unit.
items.evidence: A second word-event formula recurring inside a single symbolic-act report is not unusual for this class of unit (the loincloth act likewise carries word-event formulas at both its performance and interpretation stages, Jer.13.3 and Jer.13.8, while remaining one report); the yotser root recurs from the potter noun at Jer.18.2 and Jer.18.6 to the framing verb at Jer.18.11, binding the Judah-directed application to the observed sign rather than to a fresh discourse unit; all twelve verses of the span are prose with zero WEB poetry-line verses.

items.claim: Jer.18.13-18.17 is correctly cut from the potter unit as its own judgment_oracle on a genuine register and grammatical-person shift, not on the koh-amar alone.
items.evidence: All five verses of the span open WEB poetry lines against zero across the whole preceding Jer.18.1-12, and the address shifts from second-person address of Judah to third-person description of the virgin of Israel; the koh-amar at Jer.18.13 carries no frame-owner change by itself, so the register-and-addressee shift, not the bare formula, is the operative seam, matching how the span's own boundary reasoning frames it.

items.claim: Jer.18.18-18.23 correctly keeps the narrated plot and Jeremiah's imprecatory reply as one confession unit, since no tier-1 formula separates them and the plotters' quoted plan supplies the occasion the reply answers.
items.evidence: No koh-amar or word-event formula occurs anywhere in Jer.18.18-23; the genuine seam opening the span is the scene shift at Jer.18.18, where new speakers are narrated in the third person plotting against Jeremiah by name, distinct from the preceding third-person judgment oracle; the ketiv/qere notes at Jer.18.22 and Jer.18.23 are correctly disclosed against the MT inventory.

items.claim: Jer.19.1-19.13 correctly holds the jar-purchase command, the oracle to proclaim, the breaking performance, and the interpretation as one symbolic-act unit, closing before the genuine scene-and-addressee shift at Jer.19.14.
items.evidence: The interior koh-amar tokens at Jer.19.3 and Jer.19.11 continue the same commissioned proclamation opened at Jer.19.1 with no frame-owner change; the interior neum-YHWH formulas at Jer.19.6 and Jer.19.12 are correctly read as closure-corroborating texture rather than as a driver; Jer.19.14 relocates the scene from the valley to the court of Yahweh's house and widens the addressee from the elders taken along to all the people, byte-confirmed against the collated text as the stronger seam the span correctly stops before.
tier_citations: neum-YHWH formula inventory (tier-3, closure corroboration only)
